- Implemented server integration with the Spotify Web API and wired a UI section into your About page.

What I added
- API + utils:
  - `lib/spotify.ts`: refresh-token auth, helpers for last played and top tracks.
  - `app/api/spotify/now-playing/route.ts`: returns your last played track.
  - `app/api/spotify/top-tracks/route.ts`: returns your top tracks (supports `limit`, `time_range`).
- UI:
  - `components/spotify-music.tsx`: client component that fetches and displays last played + top 5.
  - Integrated into `app/about/page.tsx` under the Skills section.
- Styles:
  - Added Minecraft-themed styles in `app/globals.css` for the music cards.

Environment setup (required)
1) Create a Spotify app and get credentials:
- Go to `https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard`
- Create an app → grab Client ID and Client Secret
- Add a Redirect URI (use exactly): `http://localhost:3000`

2) Authorize once to obtain a code:
- Open this URL in the browser (replace `YOUR_CLIENT_ID`):
`https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&scope=user-read-recently-played%20user-top-read&redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000`
- After login/consent, you’ll be redirected to `http://localhost:3000/?code=...` — copy the code value.

3) Exchange the code for a refresh token:
- Replace placeholders (CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, CODE, REDIRECT_URI) and run:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -u CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=CODE \
  -d redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000 \
  https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token
```
- Copy `refresh_token` from the response.

4) Add env vars in `.env.local`:
```bash
SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN=your_refresh_token
```
- Restart dev server after adding these.

How to view
- Run the app and visit `/about`. The “MUSIC STATUS” section shows:
  - Last played track with album art
  - Top 5 tracks (last 4 weeks). You can change timeframe via query param on the API route (`short_term`, `medium_term`, `long_term`).

Notes
- Build completed successfully; there are only minor lint warnings.
- If you want SSR instead of client fetching, I can refactor the About page to fetch server-side.

- Added `SpotifyMusic` to `app/about/page.tsx`; created `lib/spotify.ts`, two API routes (`now-playing`, `top-tracks`), and Minecraft-styled UI in `app/globals.css`. Build passed. Set `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SPOTIFY_REFRESH_TOKEN` in `.env.local`, and you’re live.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>**Clarifying redirect URI issues**

I need to help the user with the Spotify Developer Dashboard issue regarding the redirect URI "http://localhost:3000." Spotify requires an exact match for the redirect URI, including the scheme and path, which can sometimes lead to errors. The URI must be pre-registered, and it allows http for localhost but requires the path if it's included. A few quick fixes that resolve that Spotify “Please enter a valid redirect URI” error:

- Use a full absolute URI with scheme
  - Prefer: http://localhost:3000
  - Don’t include quotes or backticks. No spaces.
- Try variants if it still complains
  - http://localhost:3000/ (trailing slash)
  - http://localhost:3000/callback (any path is fine)
  - http://127.0.0.1:3000 (IP instead of hostname)
- Click Add after typing it, then Save
- Redirect URI must match exactly in your authorize URL (and be URL-encoded there)
  - Example authorize link (note the encoded redirect_uri):
```text
https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&scope=user-read-recently-played%20user-top-read&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000
```

Common pitfalls:
- Pasting with backticks/quotes, trailing spaces, or using https://localhost (use http).
- Mismatch between what you saved (with/without trailing slash/path) and what you pass in redirect_uri.
